remainingDistance.governanceGate: This is not a free implementation. The task ledger already requires that any alternative cold-start, hierarchical or pooling method carry its own versioned model-policy decision plus untouched holdout evidence. So a decision #84 must be framed and frozen BEFORE the candidate is built and scored, or the work is unusable no matter how it performs.

remainingDistance.untriedRemedy: Shrink the cold-start estimate toward the origin-safe comparator: p50 = w * lgbm_p50 + (1-w) * cold_start_mean, with w fitted on development origins only, segmented at most by market x horizon, shrunk to parent when a segment misses the frozen sufficiency rule. Both inputs are origin-safe, so this does not leak -- unlike the assortment exit signal PP3-B6 rejected. Non-inferiority is reachable by construction as w approaches 0, while w > 0 retains whatever signal the model does carry. This changes the estimator rather than rescaling it, which is why it is a different experiment from C1 and C3 rather than a variant of them.
remainingDistance.whatHasAlreadyFailed: Five candidates rejected: C1 global bias correction (worsens WAPE because P50 is a median and WAPE is median-optimal), C2 quantile calibration (+0.000%, the gate is WAPE-only), C1+C2, C3 segmented champion factors scoped to this cohort (-0.149% all-13, -12.285% final-5), C4 hierarchical reconciliation. All five adjust a scale factor or an interval; none replaces the estimator. The champion losing to a mean-of-last-13-weeks on thin-history series is an estimator problem, so a sixth scale factor is not the next experiment.
remainingDistance.whyThisIsTheRightTarget: The cold-start cohort carries 31.9% of global error mass on 22.5% of volume, and us-new-york is 57.5% of the cold-start actual volume. It is simultaneously the largest concentrated block of addressable error in the bundle and the one gate that fails, so it is the only place where fixing the gate and improving the forecast are the same work. PP3-B3 ranked causes across the whole population, which spread this signal across category and lifecycle hypotheses; the cohort view concentrates it.

supported_os_evidence.evidence: macOS 26.5 Darwin arm64 complete. A static portability audit was run in place of the two missing hosts and found exactly one hard blocker, now fixed: datagen/src/retail_datagen/generator.py imported the POSIX-only `resource` module at module scope, which would raise ModuleNotFoundError on Windows and make datagen unimportable. Replaced by retail_datagen/process_usage.py, which keeps the POSIX reading byte-identical (verified against getrusage directly) and adds a stdlib ctypes path for Windows. Audit found clean: no POSIX signals or fork, no shell=True or /bin/sh, no hardcoded POSIX paths, no symlinks, no case-colliding tracked filenames, .gitattributes normalises all text to LF with CRLF reserved for .bat/.cmd, the CSV writer sets encoding and newline explicitly, tools/dev.py and check_isolated_wheels.py both resolve Scripts/python.exe when os.name == "nt", and the Go tree has no build tags or syscalls. A static audit is not a run: it cannot catch behavioural divergence, so the two host runs remain open evidence.
